'''Mamie Parker''' (born October 14, 1957) is an American [[biologist]], [[Conservationist (biology)|conservationist]], executive coach, facilitator, and inspirational speaker from [[Wilmot, Arkansas]]. She holds a PhD in [[limnology]] from the [[University of Wisconsin]] and spent 30 years with the [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service]] (USFWS) in a variety of positions in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Missouri, Georgia, and Washington, D.C.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> Highly regarded as a pioneer in the field, she was the first Black woman to serve as the assistant director of Fisheries and Habitat Conservation and the first African American to lead a USFWS regional office when she served as the Northeast Service Regional Director, covering 13 northeastern states.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Mamie A. Parker|url=https://chesapeakeconservancy.org/teams/dr-mamie-a-parker/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Chesapeake Conservancy|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service|date=2020|title=Conservation History: Women in Conservation|url=https://nctc.fws.gov/history/Documents/2020-Conservation-History-journal.pdf|access-date=|website=|archive-date=2020-11-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126001739/https://nctc.fws.gov/history/Documents/2020-Conservation-History-journal.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|last=Carr|first=Michelle|date=2016-06-01|title=Diversity Matters: Collaboration and Inclusivity in Conservation in Conservation|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/diversity-matters-collaboration-and-inclusivity-in_b_574f47c4e4b07f2507c94ffa|access-date=2020-07-13|website=HuffPost|language=en}}</ref> She also served as USFWS Chief of Staff and Chief of Fisheries.<ref name=":0" /> She received the US government's highest honor for career service employees for her accomplishments, the [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Rank]] Meritorious Service Award,<ref name=":2" /> and in 2005 was the first African American inducted into the Arkansas Outdoor Hall of Fame.<ref name=":9" /> Since retiring from USFWS, she has worked as an executive leadership coach, inspirational speaker, and environmental consultant with Ma Parker and Associates and EcoLogix Group, Inc.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=MA Parker & Associates|url=https://www.mamieparker.com/|access-date=2020-07-13|website=MA Parker & Associates|archive-date=2020-09-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923104552/https://www.mamieparker.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> She is on the board of directors of the [[National Wildlife Federation]], Chesapeake Bay Foundation, [[Duke University]] Nicholas School of the Environment, [[The Nature Conservancy|The Nature Conservancy-Virginia Chapter]], [[American University]] School of Public Affairs, [[Ducks Unlimited]], and the [[Student Conservation Association]]. Throughout her career she has worked to advance diversity and opportunities for minority students in conservation and fisheries careers; in 2016 she was awarded the [[Emmeline Moore]] Prize from the [[American Fisheries Society]] for these efforts.<ref name=":8" />

== Early life and education ==
Parker was born and raised in [[Wilmot, Arkansas]], the youngest of 11 children.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Mamie Aselean Parker (1957–)|url=https://encyclopediaofarkansas.net/entries/mamie-aselean-parker-4127/|access-date=2020-08-16|website=Encyclopedia of Arkansas|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Arkansas Outdoor Hall of Fame|url=https://www.agff.org/hof|access-date=2020-08-16|website=agff2020|page=4|language=en}}</ref> Her mother was a single parent and supported the family by working as a [[Sharecropping|sharecropper]].<ref name=":9" /> Her interest in the outdoors started in childhood, inspired by her mother who was an avid angler and outdoorswoman, and her interest in biology began in high school when a biology teacher introduced her to issues of environmental degradation.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2020-04-10|title=Dr. Mamie Parker, UAPB Alumna, Reflects on 30-Year Career as Pioneer in Conservation|url=https://uapbnews.wordpress.com/2020/04/10/dr-mamie-parker-uapb-alumna-reflects-on-30-year-career-as-pioneer-in-conservation/|access-date=2020-07-12|website=UAPB News|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":6" /> Parker holds a BS in biology from the [[University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff]] (UAPB), and an MS in fish and wildlife management and PhD in limnology, both from the [[University of Wisconsin–Green Bay|University of Wisconsin-Green Bay]] (UW). Her work at UW included researching ways to clean contaminants and pollutants from the Great Lakes and its tributaries.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /> She has also completed executive leadership training at the [[Harvard University]] John F. Kennedy School of Government.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==

=== United States Fish and Wildlife Service ===
Parker was inspired to join the USFWS when Hannibal Bolton, a 1971 alumnus of the UAPB, visited the university to recruit students for a USFWS internship. She completed two internships with the USFWS, one in Wisconsin and one in Minnesota. She then moved to work for USFWS in the [[Columbia, Missouri]] Ecological Services Office, where she worked on providing ecological recommendations for federal permits and projects.<ref name=":2" /> She later was reassigned to work in the [[Missouri Bootheel]] region, the Midwest regional office in Minneapolis in 1990, and the Southeastern Regional Office in Atlanta in 1996, where she was appointed Deputy Assistant Regional Director of Fisheries and Deputy Geographic Assistant Regional Director in Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":6" />

In 1998, Parker moved to Washington, D.C. to serve as Special Assistant to the deputy director and Director (now known as Chief of Staff) in the USFWS headquarters in Washington D.C. where she worked with programs in all 50 states.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":6" /> In 1999, she moved to the North Atlantic-Appalachian regional field office and served as the Northeast Regional Director, covering 13 northeastern states from Maine to Virginia and West Virginia. She was the first African American to lead as the director of a regional USFWS office in the agency's history.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|last=Martin|first=Sandra|date=2001|title=Interview with Mamie Parker|url=https://www.webpages.uidaho.edu/winr/parker.htm|access-date=2020-07-13|website=www.webpages.uidaho.edu|publisher=University of Idaho}}</ref>

In 2003, she was appointed USFWS Assistant Director of Fisheries and Habitat Conservation. She was the first Black woman to hold this position. In this position, she provided leadership on national projects, including the National Fish Habitat Action Partnership, and served as the facilitator at the White House Conference on the Environment.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> She also served as co-chair of the Aquatic Nuisance Species Task Force.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded the [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Rank Meritorious Service Award]], the highest award given to government employees, for her leadership in the creation of the National Fish Habitat Action Partnership.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" />

=== Executive consulting ===
Since retiring from the USFWS in 2007, Parker has worked as an executive leadership coach and speaker. She is a member of the [[Brown Advisory]] Sustainable Investment Board and serves as a principal consultant of EcoLogix Group, Inc. and Ma Parker and Associates.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Mamie Parker {{!}} Brown Advisory|url=https://www.brownadvisory.com/mamie-parker|access-date=2020-07-12|website=www.brownadvisory.com}}</ref> Clients include the [[Gates Millennium Scholars Program]], the [[Bureau of Land Management]], [[Defense Language Institute]], the USFWS, the [[Maryland Department of Labor]], the [[United States Department of the Interior|Department of the Interior]], [[Minnesota Department of Natural Resources]], [[Maryland Department of Transportation|Maryland Port Administration]], [[Maryland Department of Labor]], the [[Clinton Presidential Center|William J. Clinton Presidential Center]], Little Rock Central High School National Historic Site, [[National Wild Turkey Federation]], and [[Ducks Unlimited]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" />

=== Mentoring and service ===
[[File:John Cornely and Mamie Parker, two contest judges excited for the final day of judging.jpg|thumb|289x289px|Dr. Mamie Parker and John Cornely at the USFWS stamp art contest, September 2013]]
Parker is views herself as a pioneer in her field for women of color and feels a "responsibility to do well".<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|last1=Martin |first1=Michel |title=From Fishing With Mom To Becoming A Top Fisheries Official|url=https://www.npr.org/2015/07/14/421141198/from-fishing-with-mom-to-becoming-a-top-fisheries-official|access-date=2020-07-13|website=NPR.org|date=14 July 2015 |language=en}}</ref> In a 2016 address, she noted: ''"As one of very few women of color working in conservation at that time, I was a pioneer. It can be lonely when you're a pioneer, because you're all by yourself."<ref name=":4" />'' During her time at USFWS, Parker helped create Chicago Wilderness, a diverse coalition of conservation groups working to conserve areas in the [[Chicago metropolitan area]].<ref name=":4" /> While at the USFWS Northeast regional office, she helped establish the USFWS "Invest in People" mentoring and professional leadership development program, which included opportunities for administrative personnel to get outdoors and experience some of the work conducted by field biologists;<ref name=":6" /> the program was later expanded to the D.C. headquarters and other regions throughout the country.<ref name=":1" />

She has also promoted diversity in [[STEM]] by starting career awareness institutes at [[Tennessee Tech University]] and within USFWS to expose minority students from across the country to careers in fisheries.<ref name=":8" /> In her current work, she continues to help underserved communities and advance diversity and inclusion in STEM. She helps conduct Wild STEM workshops throughout the world, to expose more minority youth to careers in conservation.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> In a 2020 feature on her career, she noted:{{blockquote|''"At this point in life, I have learned more about showing gratitude by giving back. This includes work to encourage others to help us address the climate crisis, particularly in vulnerable and underserved communities, by looking for opportunities to make a profound impact on the lives of women and diverse employees in conservation by working harder on diversity, inclusion, justice and equity. Serving in nominating and governance roles on multiple boards, I recruit and retain diversity."''<ref name=":1" />}}In 2016, she was awarded the [[Emmeline Moore]] Prize from the [[American Fisheries Society]] for her work promoting diversity and opportunity for minorities in fisheries education and careers. She has written about supporting and mentoring minority students in fisheries, including a chapter entitled ''Mentoring Minorities for More Effective Fisheries Management and Conservation,'' published in ''The Future of Fisheries: Perspectives for Emerging Professionals'' by the American Fisheries Society.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Mamie Parker Receives American Fisheries Society's Emmeline Moore Prize {{!}} American Fisheries Society|url=https://fisheries.org/2016/08/dr-mamie-parker-receives-american-fisheries-societys-emmeline-moore-prize/|access-date=2020-08-16|website=fisheries.org |date=23 August 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Future of Fisheries: Perspectives for Emerging Professionals {{!}} American Fisheries Society|url=https://fisheries.org/bookstore/all-titles/professional-and-trade/55073p-2/|access-date=2020-08-16|website=fisheries.org}}</ref> On encouraging minority youth to enter conservation careers, she has said:{{blockquote|''"When I speak to youth, I tell them about my story as a pioneer conservationist and call them to action....I ask them to think about the things they can do to better their communities. Several youth have expressed interest in pursuing careers in conservation, marine biology and environmental justice, fighting the environmental inequality that communities of color often face."''<ref name=":2" />}}Parker is currently a speaker with the Diverse Environmental Leaders Speakers Bureau<ref>{{Cite web|title=Diverse Environmental Leaders - Speakers Bureau|url=https://www.delnsb.com/|access-date=2020-08-16|website=DELNSB|language=en}}</ref> and serves on the board of the [[Chesapeake Conservancy]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Board of Directors|url=https://chesapeakeconservancy.org/who-we-are/leadership/board-of-directors/|access-date=2020-08-16|website=Chesapeake Conservancy|language=en-US}}</ref> the [[National Wildlife Refuge Association]] Board of Directors Advisory Council,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Our Board|url=https://www.refugeassociation.org/board|access-date=2020-08-16|website=The National Wildlife Refuge Association|language=en-US}}</ref> [[Marstel-Day]]'s Advisory Council,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Mamie A. Parker Joins Marstel-Day's Advisory Council|url=https://www.prweb.com/releases/2011/9/prweb8820541.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110925002038/http://www.prweb.com/releases/2011/9/prweb8820541.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 25, 2011|access-date=2020-08-16|website=PRWeb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Advisory Council|url=https://www.marstel-day.com/our-company/advisory-council/|access-date=2020-08-16|website=Marstel-Day|language=en-US}}</ref> and Brown Advisory's Board of Directors on the Sustainable Investing Advisory Board.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mamie Parker {{!}} Brown Advisory|url=https://www.brownadvisory.com/mamie-parker|access-date=2020-08-16|website=www.brownadvisory.com|language=en}}</ref> She also serves or has served on the boards of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Retirees Association, [[Student Conservation Association]], The Virginia Chapter of the [[The Nature Conservancy|Nature Conservancy]], [[Duke University]]'s Nicholas School of the Environment, Duke University School of the Environment Visitors Board, the Potomac Conservancy, the [[Chesapeake Bay Foundation]], and [[Defenders of Wildlife]]. She was appointed by [[Terry McAuliffe|Governor Terry McAuliffe]] to the [[Virginia Department of Game and Inland Fisheries]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />[[File:Dr. Mamie Parker was awarded The 2020 John L. Morris Award by the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies.jpg|thumb|288x288px|Dr. Mamie Parker is the recipient of The 2020 John L. Morris Award by the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies]]

== Awards and honors ==
* Inducted into University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Hall of Fame<ref name=":2" />
* Named the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Simon Haley Distinguished Lecturer<ref name=":9" />
* The [[Council of Women World Leaders]] awarded her with an [[Aspen Institute]] Fellowship where she worked in the Kingdom of Lesotho and in Cape Town and Johannesburg, South Africa.<ref name=":0" />
* Department of Interior's Silver Award, presented by the Secretary of the USFWS<ref name=":0" />
* Member of [[Alpha Kappa Alpha]] sorority.<ref name=":2" />
* USFWS Advanced Leadership Development Program - Ira Gabrielson Leadership Award for outstanding leader of the year<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":8" />
* Presidential Rank Meritorious Service Award<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" />
* Appointed by [[Terry McAuliffe|Governor Terry McAuliffe]] to the [[Virginia Department of Game and Inland Fisheries]]<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />
* 1999: Appointed USFWS Northeast Regional Director<ref name=":6" />
* 2002: [[Good Housekeeping|''Good Housekeeping'' Magazine]] Women in Government Leadership Award<ref>{{Cite web|last=Springer|first=Craig|date=2004|title=Dr. Mamie Parker|url=https://www.webpages.uidaho.edu/winr/springer.htm|access-date=2020-08-16|website=www.webpages.uidaho.edu|series=Women in Natural Resources|publisher=U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service}}</ref><ref name=":9" />
* 2003: Appointed USFWS Assistant Director of Fisheries and Habitat Conservation<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />
* 2005: Inducted into the Arkansas Outdoor Hall of Fame<ref name=":9" />
* 2015: Champion of the Chesapeake from [[Chesapeake Conservancy]]<ref name=":0" />
* 2016: Emmeline Moore Prize from the American Fisheries Society for "exemplary service to the cause of equal opportunity of access to higher education in fisheries and/or professional development in any of the disciplines of fisheries science or management"<ref name=":8" />
* 2018: William K. Reilly Environmental Leadership Award from [[American University School of Public Affairs]]' Center for Environmental Policy<ref name=":0" />
*2020: Recipient of The 2020 John L. Morris Award by the Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies<ref>{{Cite web|title=Department of Wildlife Resources Board Member Receives Prestigious John L. Morris Award {{!}} Virginia DWR|url=https://dwr.virginia.gov/blog/department-of-wildlife-resources-board-member-receives-prestigious-john-l-morris-award/|access-date=2020-12-11|language=en}}</ref>
